newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ING says Brazil's Coelce shares cheap.
newsitem.headline: ING says Brazil's Coelce shares cheap.

text.p: ING Barings said Brazilian state-owned electricity distributor Coelce has good growth potential and its shares are cheap compared with similar power firms.
"The stocks valuation looks quite cheap," ING Barings analyst Charles Barnett said in a report.
He compared Coelba's earnings per megawatt-hour (MWh) sold of $151 with Coelba ($189) and Cerj ($195), "which have similar operating regions."
Coelce, which is slated to be privatized in 1998's first quarter, is owned by the government of the fast-growing northeastern state of Ceara.

"We view Ceara as an attractive operating region for electricity distribution," the report said. "Not only is there a booming tourist industry, but the state has the fastest-growing industrial park in northeastern Brazil."
Coelce's sales grew 11 percent in 1996, well above the national average of six percent, while its energy losses of 13.3 percent were below Cerj, Coelba and Light, it added.
The state on May 5 plans to auction off a 15-percent stake in Coelce as an initial step toward privatizing the firm and to create a more-liquid market for the shares.
Coelce's preferred A share was up 1.22 percent at 1554 local/1854 GMT on the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa).
